extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multilingual speech representations across speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval, covering 102 languages and including the new Fleurs dataset.
extraction.license: Tasks should be available under a permissive license that allows the use and redistribution of the data for research purposes.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S combines several existing multilingual speech datasets and introduces Fleurs, for which the authors collected recordings of parallel sentences and created train/dev/test splits.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is more than 97% complete, with some missing recordings and some low-quality recordings that may be replaced in a future version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark uses public datasets including FLoRes dev/devtest sentences for Fleurs recordings, MLS from Librivox audiobooks, VoxPopuli from European Parliament sessions, CoVoST-2 for speech translation, and MINDS-14 for spoken intent classification.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors created new train/dev/test splits for Fleurs, merged monolingual MINDS-14 datasets into a multilingual dataset, and provide scripts to reproduce preprocessing when needed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, speech recordings were collected for parallel sentences from FLoRes; benchmark labels come from the underlying tasks such as ASR transcriptions, translations, language IDs, and intent labels from the source datasets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: between one and three recordings per sentence (2.3 on average)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A second version of FLEURS may include fixes for missing or low-quality recordings, and updates will be made on the platform.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by making speech technology available in all languages, especially under-represented ones, to give speakers an equal voice on the Internet and help share their content and culture.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance differs substantially across geographical language groups, with better results on Western European languages partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data in those languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on linguistic aspects of speech and does not evaluate nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects such as speech synthesis or voice conversion; speech classification tasks are also prone to overfitting.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for evaluation of multilingual speech representations across ASR, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval, with fine-tuning scripts and public access through Hugging Face.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S, a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We note that the tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated.
